_meta.purpose: The only register of factual claims this project is allowed to make. Every table row on the site points at one of these ids.
_meta.rule: verification=primary-full means the page was fetched and the clause text read in this session. primary-snippet means an official page surfaced in search results and was not re-fetched here. secondary-only means no official page was retrieved. Values that no row supports are left blank on the site and flagged.

sources.claim: Associates must clearly and prominently state, on the site, the exact sentence: "As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases."
sources.section: Associates Program Operating Agreement, Section 5 (Identifying Yourself as an Associate); agreement updated October 15, 2025
sources.quote: You must clearly and prominently state the following, or any substantially similar statement previously allowed under this Agreement, on your Site ...: “As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.”
sources.note: Same section: violation of Section 5 is deemed a material breach (Section 6, last paragraph).

sources.claim: Links must use the special tagged link formats Amazon provides ("Special Links") and must properly use them.
sources.section: Operating Agreement, Section 1
sources.quote: The links must properly use the special “tagged” link formats we provide and comply with this Agreement (“Special Links”).

sources.claim: Special Links must use the Associates ID assigned to the account, must be accessed directly from the site, and the tag (format XXXXX-##) must appear as a URL parameter on every link to an Amazon Site.
sources.section: Associates Program Participation Requirements, Section 2(a) and 2(b)
sources.quote: You must not encourage customers to bookmark your Special Links. All Special Links must be accessed directly from your Site. For example, you must include your Associates ID or “tag” (appearing as XXXXX-##, or such other format as we may designate) as a parameter in the URL of each link you place on your Site to an Amazon Site.

sources.claim: Purchases referred by a Redirecting Link (indirect via an intermediate site without an affirmative click there) are disqualified, and purchases whose links are not properly formatted are disqualified.
sources.section: Associates Program Commission Income Statement, Section 2 (Disqualified Purchases), items (e) and (g)
sources.quote: (e) any Product purchased by a customer who is referred to an Amazon Site by a link that sends users indirectly to an Amazon Site via an intermediate site, without requiring the customer to click on a link or take some other affirmative action on that intermediate site (a “Redirecting Link”) ... (g) any Product purchase that is not correctly tracked or reported because the links from your site to the relevant Amazon Site are not properly formatted
sources.note: This is the clause that makes the supplied short links a question rather than a formality: the risk is loss of commission, not a stylistic preference.

sources.claim: Shorteners/intermediate links are prohibited when they make it unclear that the link goes to an Amazon Site, and cloaking/obscuring the site URL is prohibited.
sources.section: Participation Requirements, Section 6(v) and 6(w)
sources.quote: (w) You will not use a link shortening service, button, hyperlink or other ad placement in a manner that makes it unclear that you are linking to an Amazon Site.
sources.note: The prohibition is on obscuring the destination, not on short links per se. This is why FLG-003 stays unresolved: the test is how the link is presented and whether the tag survives.

sources.claim: A site may show prices and availability only if Amazon serves the link containing that data, or the data was obtained via Creators API / PA API and used per the License; comparison layouts have an additional lowest-new/used-price requirement.
sources.section: Participation Requirements, Section 2(b) (prices and availability paragraph)
sources.quote: your Site may only show prices and availability if: (a) we serve the link in which that price and availability data are displayed, or (b) you obtain Product pricing and availability data via Creators API or PA API and you comply with the requirements regarding use of Creators API or PA API in the License
used_by: no price columns on the site

sources.claim: Customer reviews and star ratings may not be displayed unless obtained through Creators API / PA API and used per the License.
sources.section: Participation Requirements, Section 6(t)
sources.quote: You will not display or otherwise use any of our customer reviews or star ratings, in part or in whole, on your Site unless you have obtained a link to that customer review or star rating through Creators API or PA API and you comply with the requirements for Creators API and PA API described in the License.
used_by: no rating columns on the site

sources.claim: Program Content images may not be stored or cached; only a link to the image may be stored, for up to 24 hours. Other Product Advertising Content may be cached for up to 24 hours and must then be refreshed. Individual ASINs may be stored indefinitely.
sources.section: Associates Program IP License and Usage Requirements, Section 2(h)
sources.quote: You will not store or cache Product Advertising Content consisting of an image, but you may store a link to Product Advertising Content consisting of an image for up to 24 hours. ... you may store individual Amazon Standard Identification Numbers (ASINs) for an indefinite period until the termination of this License.

sources.claim: If pricing/availability is displayed from API or Data Feed data, a date/time stamp must sit adjacent to it, together with the specified price-accuracy disclaimer; text Program Content requires the "CERTAIN CONTENT THAT APPEARS ... COMES FROM AMAZON" disclaimer in plain view.
sources.section: IP License, Section 2(i) and 2(k)
sources.quote: You will include a date/time stamp adjacent to your display of pricing or availability information ... “CERTAIN CONTENT THAT APPEARS [IN THIS APPLICATION or ON THIS SITE, as applicable] COMES FROM AMAZON. THIS CONTENT IS PROVIDED ‘AS IS’ AND IS SUBJECT TO CHANGE OR REMOVAL AT ANY TIME.”

sources.claim: Program Content may not be used to develop or improve large-language, multimodal or machine-learning models, and Product Advertising Content may not be aggregated, analysed, extracted or repurposed without Amazon's express prior written approval.
sources.section: IP License, Section 1 (final paragraph) and Section 2(e)
sources.quote: You will not, and will not allow any third party to, use Program Content to, directly or indirectly, develop or improve large language or multimodal models, machine learning models or related technology. ... (e) You will not, without our express prior written approval, access or use Creators API, PA API or Data Feeds for the purpose of aggregating, analyzing, extracting, or repurposing any Product Advertising Content ...
sources.note: Also Participation Requirements Section 5: Special Links / Program Content may not be used to develop machine learning models or related technology without prior written approval.
used_by: scope limit on the automation brief

sources.claim: Agents (software acting autonomously on someone's behalf) may only access Program Content if they identify themselves in the User-Agent string as "Agent/[agent name]", do not mimic human interaction patterns, answer human-vs-machine prompts truthfully, and do not circumvent access controls.
sources.section: IP License, Section 4 (Agent Terms) 4(a)-(c)
sources.quote: No Agent may access, use, or interact with Program Content unless, at all times, it identifies itself ... “Agent/[agent name]” ... Not conceal or obfuscate that any access, use, or interactions are from an Agent, such as by (a) mimicking the speed or pattern of human keystrokes, page navigation, or other interactions or (b) completing or circumventing CAPTCHAs
sources.note: This section is the reason the crawler/scraper half of a generic 'AI affiliate agent' brief cannot be built as-is; the pipeline in tools/ does not touch Amazon pages at all.

sources.claim: Artificially generating clicks or impressions on your site, or creating Amazon sessions, is prohibited; and you may not purchase Products through your own Special Links or ask others to.
sources.section: Participation Requirements, Section 6(s) and 6(u)
sources.quote: (s) You will not artificially generate clicks or impressions on your Site or create Sessions on an Amazon Site, whether by way of a robot or software program or otherwise. ... (u) You will not directly or indirectly purchase any Product(s) or take a Bounty Event action through Special Links, whether for your use or for the use of any other person or entity ...
sources.note: Two direct design consequences: the click counter must only record real user interactions (no prefetch/synthetic pings), and a 'test purchase' cannot be used as the conversion check.

sources.claim: The site must not have price tracking and/or price alerting functionality unless otherwise agreed by Amazon.
sources.section: Participation Requirements, Section 6(y)
sources.quote: (y) Unless otherwise agreed by Amazon, your Site must not have price tracking and/or price alerting functionality.

sources.claim: Program Content may not be used with data mining, robots or similar data-gathering/extraction tools, and may not be redistributed or used outside the site.
sources.section: IP License, Section 1
sources.quote: This license does not include any downloading, copying or other use of Program Content for the benefit of any third party, or any use of data mining, robots, or similar data gathering and extraction tools.
used_by: why there is no Amazon scraper in tools/

sources.claim: Special Links must link to Products (as defined in the Products Statement); linking to product lists (search results, department pages, events) requires additional original content relevant to the link; mentions of limited-time promotions must be removed as soon as the promotion ends.
sources.section: Participation Requirements, Section 2(b)
sources.quote: Special Links must link to Products (as defined in the Products Statement). When linking to pages with Product lists you must have additional original content on your Site that is relevant to the Special Link. ... You must remove from your Site any links and related references to limited time promotions as soon as that promotion on the relevant Amazon Site ends.
used_by: compliance gate CHK-10 (expiry stamps on seasonal pages)

sources.claim: Inaccurate, overbroad, deceptive or otherwise misleading claims about a Product, an Amazon Site, or policies/promotions/prices are prohibited, and Program Content may not be altered except resizing/trimming that does not change meaning.
sources.section: Participation Requirements Section 2(b) (misleading-claims paragraph) and Section 6(a) (no alteration)
sources.quote: You must not make inaccurate, overbroad, deceptive or otherwise misleading claims about any Product, an Amazon Site, or any of our policies, promotions, or prices.

sources.claim: Participation requires 3 qualifying sales within 180 days of application; the application can be withdrawn if there are not enough qualifying sales in that window, and an account closed for dormancy cannot be reinstated.
sources.section: Associates Central Help, 'Account Dormancy'
sources.quote: Once you’ve applied, you have 180 days to refer a sale through one of your Associates links. Once you have referred three qualifying sales, we'll evaluate your application within a day or two and reply to you with our decision. ... You are welcome to reapply when you have established your site.
sources.note: This is the hard deadline that governs sequencing: content that can convert has to exist before the 180-day clock is wasted.

sources.claim: Qualifying purchases are measured in a session that begins at the Special Link click and ends at the earlier of 24 hours, an order for a non-digital product, or a click through another associate's link; cart completion within 89 days still counts; the product must ship/stream and be paid for within 180 days of purchase.
sources.section: Commission Income Statement, Section 1(b), 1(c)(i), 1(c)(iii)
sources.quote: (x) 24 hours elapse from that click ... completing the order for that Product no later than 89 days after their initial click-through of the Special Link ... within 180 days of the purchase, the Product is shipped to, streamed or downloaded by, and paid for by the customer
used_by: measurement page (what a 'click' can and cannot predict)
why the ledger reports orders, not revenue forecasts

sources.claim: The site owner is responsible for satisfying applicable advertising law, expressly including the U.S. FTC Guides Concerning the Use of Endorsement and Testimonials in Advertising, and for disclosing cookie/pixel use.
sources.section: Participation Requirements, Section 3(b) and 3(e)
sources.quote: including those related to disclosures (for example, if applicable, the U.S. FTC Guides Concerning the Use of Endorsement and Testimonials in Advertising) ... (e) disclosing on your Site accurately and adequately ... the use of cookies, pixels, and other technologies by you and third parties

sources.claim: FTC: a connection between endorser and marketer that a significant minority of consumers would not expect, and that would affect how they weigh the endorsement, must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously; the Endorsement Guides were revised in 2023 with a new definition of 'clearly and conspicuously'.
sources.section: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking, introduction
sources.quote: the Guides say, if there’s a connection between an endorser and the marketer that a significant minority of consumers wouldn’t expect and it would affect how they evaluate the endorsement, that connection should be disclosed clearly and conspicuously.
sources.note: The FAQ page points to 16 CFR Part 255 (source: 88 FR 48102, July 26, 2023) for the definitions themselves.

sources.claim: The Endorsement Guides are codified at 16 CFR Part 255, published at 88 FR 48102 (July 26, 2023), which is where the 'clear and conspicuous' definition and the affiliate examples live.
sources.section: 16 CFR 255.0 (Purpose and definitions); Part 255 authority 15 U.S.C. 41-58
sources.quote: Source: 88 FR 48102, July 26, 2023, unless otherwise noted. (page header: 'This content is from the eCFR and is authoritative but unofficial.')
sources.note: The section index and citation were retrieved; the full paragraph text of 255.0(f) was not captured in this session, so site copy cites the rule by number and quotes the FTC FAQ wording instead of inventing a quotation.

sources.claim: Google asks sites participating in affiliate programs to qualify affiliate links with rel="sponsored" (regardless of manual or dynamic creation); failing to qualify them can lead to manual or algorithmic action. rel="sponsored" marks ads and paid placements and is preferred over nofollow.
sources.section: Qualify outbound links to Google; and Search Central blog 'A reminder on qualifying links and our link spam update' (2021-07-26)
sources.quote: Mark links that are advertisements or paid placements (commonly called paid links) with the sponsored value. ... We ask sites participating in affiliate programs to qualify these links with rel="sponsored", regardless of whether these links were created manually or dynamically.
sources.note: The blog quote came from the search result for https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2021/07/link-tagging-and-link-spam-update; not re-fetched in this session.
used_by: rel attribute on every outbound link

sources.claim: Product rich results: Product snippets require one of review, aggregateRating or offers; product rich results only support pages focused on a single product (or its variants), not product-list or category pages; editorial reviews can use positiveNotes/negativeNotes.
sources.section: Product snippet (Product, Review, Offer) structured data — Guidelines / Technical guidelines
sources.quote: Currently, product rich results only support pages that focus on a single product (or multiple variants of the same product). ... Product snippets require either review or aggregateRating or offers
sources.note: Because no review/aggregateRating/offer data can be lawfully held here without API access, the build emits Product markup only when a product row is confirmed, and otherwise emits Article + FAQPage markup. No fake ratings are emitted.

sources.claim: Publishing a static site to GitHub Pages from Actions means: job permissions pages:write and id-token:write, actions/configure-pages, actions/upload-pages-artifact pointing at the built folder, and actions/deploy-pages in a job bound to the 'github-pages' environment.
sources.section: Using custom workflows with GitHub Pages — Configuring the upload-pages-artifact action / Deploying GitHub Pages artifacts
sources.quote: The job must have a minimum of pages: write and id-token: write permissions. ... An environment must be established to enforce branch/deployment protection rules. The default environment is github-pages.

sources.claim: Amazon's Associates software automatically appends "-20" to Associate IDs; separate tracking IDs are created under 'Manage your Tracking IDs', and are the mechanism for reporting on multiple sites or links.
sources.section: Help: 'Can I change my Associates ID?' and 'Managing Multiple Web Sites' glossary
sources.quote: We are unable to change your Associates ID. Please note that our software automatically adds “-20” to the end of all Associate IDs. If you would like a different tracking ID to appear in your links, please visit Manage your Tracking IDs to create tracking IDs for your Associates account.
sources.note: Used only to explain why the given tracking ID ends in -20 and why 'shopnow047c' is the implied Associates ID. The account's actual ownership of that ID is unverified here — see Q-02.

sources.claim: The identifier syntax used to point at one product on Amazon is /dp/<ASIN> on the marketplace's own domain; an ASIN is Amazon's item identifier, and Product lists (search results, departments, events) are treated differently from Products.
sources.section: Participation Requirements, Section 2(b) (Product / Product list definitions)
sources.quote: Product lists include search results, events (e.g. Prime Day), or a department homepage (e.g. grocery).
sources.note: No official Amazon page defining the ASIN as '10 characters' was retrievable from this session, so the intake tool reports the observed character count and flags the mismatch instead of asserting a rule. See FLG-002.

sources.claim: Google's spam policies treat 'thin affiliation' — affiliate pages whose product descriptions are copied from the merchant with no original content or added value, often cookie-cutter across a network — as a violation; good affiliate pages add original reviews, comparison, navigation and price information.
sources.section: Spam policies for Google web search — Thin content / site reputation and third-party content; earlier wording at /search/docs/advanced/guidelines/affiliate-programs
sources.quote: Affiliate pages can be considered thin if they are a part of a program that distributes its content across a network of affiliates without providing additional value. These sites often appear as cookie-cutter sites or templates ... Good affiliate sites add value by offering meaningful content or features.
sources.note: This is the single most important reason the site publishes original question-shaped guides rather than generated product descriptions, and the reason the project does not mass-generate articles.

sources.claim: A sitemap file is a supported way to tell search engines about a site's URLs, and it must list canonical URLs of indexable pages; feeds/sitemaps are separate files referenced from robots.txt.
sources.section: Introduction to sitemaps for web developers
sources.note: Not re-fetched in this session. Treated as background, not as a source for any displayed claim; the sitemap is generated from data and validated for well-formedness by tools/check_site.py rather than for policy conformance.
